output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not mainly the new starters. That change cut the credit agents can apply on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and sent to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at 82%, and neither figure changed. Billing FCR fell from 79% to 56%. The referral rate is the same for April-intake agents (56%) and for tenured agents (53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount as the site. The new starters are slightly lower (66.4%), but they are not the driver. Tariff enquiries rose but still resolve at 85%. The IVR change came two weeks later, after the drop had already happened. Do not put new starters on performance plans. It would punish the wrong group and rest on a site-wide number. Next, agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Pair it with post-call sampling of credits, which is the control Finance has said it would accept, and track FCR and unsupported credits. Extend that to the whole site only if the trial holds. I'm fairly confident in this. The remaining gaps are the share of the fall caused by the referral change and any workload effect, which the trial would show.
